claim: Japan's Ministry of Munitions was formed on 1 November 1943 to unify the production of arms, aircraft above all
note: That the Army and Navy had each run their own aircraft factories and designs and bid against each other for aluminum and engines is from memory and unchecked. That aircraft output rose through 1944 while the supply of pilots lagged is from memory.

claim: On 21 October 1943 students marched in the rain at the Meiji Jingu Gaien stadium before Tojo; the deferment of university students had ended (decision 21 September, imperial ordinance 2 October) and the first were called up from December
source: Waseda University History Museum; Hosei University; Hokkaido Shimbun; Unseen Japan
note: Crowd figures run from 25,000 to 70,000 and the report gives none. That students entered the flying schools and schoolgirls replaced them in factories is from memory.

claim: American submarines sank Japanese merchant ships, tankers among them, faster than they were replaced; the Navy formed an independent escort command in November 1943
source: Interrogation of Japanese naval officers (USSBS) via ww2db.com: 'independent Combined Escort Fleet in November 1943'; Wikipedia, Hi convoys
note: The command's name differs between sources (Combined Escort Fleet, Grand Escort Command); the report does not name it.

claim: Tojo was removed as Chief of the Army General Staff on 16 July 1944 and the cabinet announced its resignation on 18 July; Koiso Kuniaki succeeded on 22 July
source: Wikipedia, Hideki Tojo and Kuniaki Koiso; JACAR timeline
note: The report says Tojo resigned 'as Prime Minister and as Chief of the Army General Staff' on 18 July: the sources give the staff post as 16 July. To correct in the next pass.

claim: Saipan fell in the first days of July 1944; a Supreme Council for the Direction of the War was formed in August 1944 in place of the Liaison Conferences used since November 1937
source: From memory; a court exhibit shows the Supreme War Directing Conference meeting on 15 September 1944
note: No source found for the August date or for the replacement. To be checked.

claim: The 1945 rice crop was poor (the worst in about four decades, by Japanese press at the end of 1945); imports from Korea, Taiwan and Indochina had fallen to almost nothing by the summer; the city ration had been cut
source: Dartmouth Press Translations (Japanese press, December 1945); Wikipedia, Food during the occupation of Japan
note: The report says the ministries told the cabinet the food would not last into the winter: from memory and unchecked.

claim: USS Essex was commissioned on 31 December 1942 and reached the Pacific in mid-1943 with Yorktown (CV-10); more of the class followed through 1943
note: The names and dates of the other ships of the class were not read. That the 1942 losses were replaced faster than Japan replaced its own is from memory.

claim: Landing ships tank were the bottleneck on Allied amphibious operations in 1943 and 1944; the Atlantic and Normandy took priority
source: JCS planning paper, FRUS 1943 d524; USNI Naval History, 'Normandy's Crucial Component'; HistoryNet
note: Sources cover 1942 to 1943 and Normandy; how the shortage bore on the Pacific in early 1944 is stated generally.

claim: On 25 October 1944 the escort carrier St. Lo was sunk by a kamikaze Zero of the Shikishima unit off Samar, the first major warship sunk by a kamikaze
source: Wikipedia, USS St. Lo; National WWII Museum; USNI Naval History
note: That the attacks went on over Leyte Gulf in the days that followed is from memory.

claim: Roosevelt died at Warm Springs, Georgia, on 12 April 1945; Truman was sworn in that evening and had not been told of the atomic bomb
source: History.com; Defense Media Network; Atomic Archive

claim: Combat stress caused very large numbers of psychiatric casualties at Okinawa
source: GlobalSecurity, Battle of Okinawa; Warfare History Network, 'Combat fatigue'
note: The sources are about the whole campaign, Army and Marine included. That ships on the picket stations were at general quarters for much of every day, and that the Navy relieved ships on the stations by turn, is from memory and unchecked.
